title: How should you prepare for case interviews if you have six weeks or more?
description: Starting from zero? A simple, realistic plan for 42 days of case interview prep, with what to do each week.
hook: Starting from scratch with six weeks or more? Good. You have time to build real skill rather than cramming. Here is how to use it.
body:
The plan

  1. Weeks 1 and 2: course, frameworks and glossary; easy cases
  2. Weeks 3 and 4: four or five cases a week, every drill, the case types
  3. Weeks 5 and 6: hard cases, friends twice a week, fit stories, rest the day before

Focused sprints to slot in

When one skill feels weak, give it a short burst of attention. These sprints fit inside any plan.

  • Structure & hypothesis: 30 structure drills in 5 days. 2-minute timer, draw a full structure, compare it to a model answer. Use the free structuring drill.
  • Maths & charts: 30 chart reads in 5 days + 10 min speed maths daily. 90 seconds per chart: title, axes, footnote, 2 insights, so-what. Use the free chart drill and case maths drill.
  • Recommendation: 10 recorded 60-second syntheses in 5 days. Record, play back, count filler words, re-record answer-first.
  • Clarify & recap: 20 case openings in 5 days. Only the first 3 minutes of a case: recap + 3 questions. Partner grades you.
  • Case leadership: 5 cases where you announce the next step after EVERY answer. Partner puts a tally mark each time you wait to be told where to go.
  • Communication: 7 days of Voice exercises + 1 recorded full case. See these speaking exercises.

If you fall behind

You will miss a day. Everyone does. Do not try to catch up by doubling the next day; just pick up where the plan is today. Consistency over weeks matters far more than any single session.
outro: Set your interview date on PrepForCase and your home page will show which step of the plan you are on. Next in this topic: Can you prepare for case interviews without a business background?
